promise: Bring a proven capability to the host you use.
audience: Developers bringing an observed donor capability into one or more existing hosts.
trigger: Use for a bounded capability transfer across architectures or languages, while keeping host boundaries intact.

modes.name: Gap check
modes.when: A donor seems useful but host overlap is unclear.
modes.output: Observed donor contract and an explicit keep/drop rationale per host.

modes.name: Re-express
modes.when: A missing capability and host seam are known.
modes.output: A native host slice with tests, real-surface probe, and CI parity.

modes.name: Verify
modes.when: The builder reports a transfer complete.
modes.output: A donor-derived check, bounded reopen, and retained evidence or blocker.

examples.title: A client feature with a server prerequisite
examples.brief: A fictional donor lets users pause a job; two target clients lack it and their shared runtime has no pause operation.
examples.before: Copy donor code into both clients and mark two features complete.
examples.after: Describe pause/resume behavior, add the runtime protocol first, then implement each client in its own seam and test actual state transitions.
examples.why: The capability crosses hosts through an explicit contract; client UI cannot manufacture backend behavior.

boundaries: The donor is read-only; transfer observable behavior by re-expression, not source grafting.
Existing host conventions and authority boundaries win over donor implementation choices.
Optional HGT graphs, ledgers, Forge, and Amplifier are execution aids; declared fitness is not benefit evidence.

verification.name: Ledger ratchet detector
verification.evidence: Builder/verifier state regressions rejected and synthetic fixture curve read. No new donor-host transfer or user benefit claimed.
verification.expected: The stated scope passes; no broader result inferred.

verification.name: Executable graph syntax
verification.evidence: Both retained graphs parse. No graph/orchestration changes or paid pipeline execution.
verification.expected: The stated scope passes; no broader result inferred.

verification.name: Portable packaging and install
verification.command: python3 scripts/capability.py build; python3 scripts/capability.py check; python3 scripts/capability.py doctor; python3 scripts/capability.py install --dest <temporary-parent> (twice)
verification.expected: Byte-identical canonical ZIP and isolated idempotent install.
verification.evidence: All operations passed. No runtime activation or effectiveness measured.

verification.name: Skill discovery metadata
verification.expected: Valid required frontmatter, naming, and complete scaffold.
verification.evidence: Skill is valid. This is a structural check, not a behavioral benchmark.

sources.role: Primary history and engine retained; methods consolidated behind the canonical portable entry.

evidence_summary: Retained graph syntax and ledger regression fixtures pass, and the portable install is checked. A ledger state is not donor-host equivalence; a real transfer still needs its source-derived and actual-surface evidence.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Bring the behavior to the app you use.
marketing.lead: A skill for moving a bounded capability between applications. Understand the donor, check what the host already does and rebuild the missing behavior through the host’s own architecture.

benefits.title: Transfer the useful part
benefits.body: Describe the behavior and failure paths, then drop features the host already has or does not need.

benefits.title: Keep the host coherent
benefits.body: Re-express the capability through native interfaces instead of grafting donor source into a different system.

benefits.title: Verify against the donor
benefits.body: Use donor-derived acceptance checks and actual host surfaces to challenge the builder’s completion claim.

walkthrough.title: Compare donor and host
walkthrough.detail: Observe the behavior, inspect both architectures and record the genuine gap.

walkthrough.title: Build through the host’s seams
walkthrough.detail: Land shared backend prerequisites first, then one bounded client slice with normal CI and a real-surface probe.

walkthrough.title: Verify the transferred behavior
walkthrough.detail: Derive checks from the donor, preserve gaps and hand over evidence and rollback.

use_when: A feature in another app would be useful in yours.
The same capability must reach several different clients.
A UI feature depends on a missing shared protocol operation.
not_for: Copying or vendoring donor implementation as a shortcut.
Rebuilding an entire application; use Migrate for that scope.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Transfer to compare pause/resume behavior in this fictional donor with two host clients. Keep donor source read-only. Identify current host overlap and shared runtime prerequisites, then propose one donor-derived acceptance probe per slice.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional transfer: pause a job
Donor contract: running → paused → resumed
Runtime prerequisite: explicit pause/resume operation
Client A: wire existing control
Client B: add control through native UI seam
Verification: observe state transitions in each host
State: gap checked; implementation not yet verified
marketing.proof_summary: Retained graph syntax and ledger regression fixtures pass, and the portable install is checked. A ledger state is not donor-host equivalence; a real transfer still needs its source-derived and actual-surface evidence.
marketing.next_step: Bring one donor capability and the host where you want it to work.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.

name: amplifier-capability-transfer
version_basis: No project version recorded; version remains null. The shared portable installer selects source with an explicit full Git commit; legacy and native routes follow their own documentation.

portable_method.name: transfer
portable_method.contract: Agent Skills directory; caller applies the method; no independent execution loop is installed.

portable.input: Caller task and explicitly authorized context
portable.output: Bring a proven capability to the host you use.
portable.failure: Report insufficient evidence, unsupported context or host limitation; never turn discovery into an execution claim.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

runtime.status: Host/caller authorizes each operation; installation is not a tool allowlist or standing approval.

Optional HGT graphs, ledgers, Forge, and Amplifier are execution aids; declared fitness is not benefit evidence.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Two buttons. Zero pauses.
film.blurb: In 70 seconds, Tilly the long job cannot stop, and copying another app's pause button changes nothing, because there is no pause underneath. Transfer watches what the button does, checks what your apps already have, builds the shared pause first, then lets each app add it in its own style. Until the donor's test runs in each real app, the card says not verified. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The apps, the job and the run are a fictional example. The film shows how the skill behaves; it does not report results.

shared_portable.applies_when: portable_method is declared; otherwise describe native interfaces without executing installation
guarantees: Tracked portable source membership and source-byte checks

legacy_repository.documentation: Existing install_commands and repository installation documentation, where provided.
legacy_repository.source_policy: Operator-controlled current working-tree copy. It can include untracked files and can operate outside a Git checkout; no uniform Git pin or SHA-256 transaction receipt is enforced.
legacy_repository.permissions: Review the specific command and destination; shared-installer transaction and permission guarantees do not describe this route.

native.documentation: interfaces.native, runtime_install_commands and project installation documentation, where provided.
native.source_policy: Native packaging, host composition and download routes retain their own version and provenance rules; shared portable receipt guarantees do not automatically apply.
native.permissions: Package builds may execute build tools; dependency or artifact downloads may use the network. Review the documented command, dependencies, destination and runtime authorization separately.
